microtheory.name: enactivism
microtheory.definition: The Embodied Mind tradition. Cognition as enactment of a world through coupled action. Varela + Thompson + Rosch 1991. Autopoiesis (Maturana), sense-making, value, participatory + sensorimotor + radical enactivism. Substrate analogue: substrate's babble-as-grounding + autopoietic self-modification IS enactivism.

concepts.name: embodied_mind
concepts.definition: Varela + Thompson + Rosch 1991. The book founding enactivism. Mind is bodily activity. Substrate analogue: substrate's foundational text-analogue.

concepts.name: enaction
concepts.definition: Cognition as enactment of meaningful world through action. Not representation. Substrate analogue: substrate's action-grounded meaning.

concepts.name: autopoiesis_enactivism
concepts.definition: Maturana + Varela 1972. Self-production. Living system produces + maintains its own components. Substrate analogue: substrate's self-modification + persistence.

concepts.name: structural_coupling
concepts.definition: Maturana + Varela. Persistent reciprocal interaction between system + environment. No representation needed. Substrate analogue: substrate-world coupling.

concepts.name: sense_making
concepts.definition: Living systems make sense of environment through their own organization. Value emerges from autopoiesis. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-based interpretation.

concepts.name: intrinsic_normativity
concepts.definition: Living systems have inherent norms — keep living. Foundation of value. Weber + Varela. Substrate analogue: substrate's self-preservation drives.

concepts.name: value_in_living
concepts.definition: Living systems generate value from need to persist. Substrate analogue: substrate's drives as inherent values.

concepts.name: operational_closure
concepts.definition: Maturana + Varela. System's organization makes reference only to itself. Closed in operations but open to perturbation. Substrate analogue: substrate's introspective closure.

concepts.name: organizational_closure
concepts.definition: Cycle of processes producing components that produce the cycle. Substrate analogue: substrate's self-modification loop.

concepts.name: sensorimotor_enactivism
concepts.definition: O'Regan + Noë 2001. Perception is mastery of sensorimotor contingencies. Phenomenal character explained by mastery. Substrate analogue: substrate's action-coupled perception.

concepts.name: radical_enactivism
concepts.definition: Hutto + Myin 2012. Cognition basic level entirely contentless. No internal representation. Substrate analogue: substrate's lowest-level non-representational dynamics.

concepts.name: participatory_sense_making
concepts.definition: De Jaegher + Di Paolo 2007. Social cognition through coordinated interaction. Substrate analogue: substrate-substrate interactive cognition.

concepts.name: embodied_dynamical_system
concepts.definition: Cognition as continuous dynamics in agent-environment system. Substrate analogue: substrate's continuous Mt-state dynamics.

concepts.name: coupled_dynamical_system
concepts.definition: Two systems whose dynamics influence each other reciprocally. Substrate analogue: substrate-world coupled equations.

concepts.name: attractor_landscape_enactivism
concepts.definition: Cognition flows through attractor landscape. Categorical perception, decisions. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin landscape.

concepts.name: phenomenology_enactivism
concepts.definition: Husserl + Merleau-Ponty + Varela. Lived experience as data + ground. Substrate analogue: substrate's introspective data.

concepts.name: lived_body
concepts.definition: Merleau-Ponty. Phenomenology of own body as subject, not object. Substrate analogue: substrate's first-person self-model.

concepts.name: neurophenomenology
concepts.definition: Varela 1996. Combining phenomenological + neural analysis. Substrate analogue: substrate's introspective + structural combined.

concepts.name: minimal_self_enactivism
concepts.definition: Zahavi. Pre-reflective first-person givenness. Substrate analogue: substrate's pre-reflective self-organization.

concepts.name: evolution_of_cognition
concepts.definition: Cognition evolved from autopoiesis through increasingly complex sense-making. Substrate analogue: substrate's developmental progression.

concepts.name: extended_evolutionary_psychology
concepts.definition: Cognition shaped by reciprocal evolution of brain + body + environment. Substrate analogue: substrate's co-evolution.

concepts.name: interactional_loop
concepts.definition: Tight reciprocal coupling between agent + world. Foundation of enactive cognition. Substrate analogue: substrate's babble + correction loop.

concepts.name: world_as_lived
concepts.definition: World as it appears in agent's enactment, not as objective external. Substrate analogue: substrate's enacted-world model.

concepts.name: anti_representationalism_enactive
concepts.definition: Cognition doesn't require internal representations matching external world. Substrate analogue: substrate's direct-dynamic interpretation.

concepts.name: constitutive_versus_causal_role
concepts.definition: Body + environment CONSTITUTE cognition, not just cause it. Substrate analogue: substrate's body-graph as constitutive.

rules.name: enaction_replaces_representation
rules.head: the substrate is cognitive in the enactive sense
rules.body: cognition is enactment via coupling with environment, not internal representation of external world. Varela. Substrate's enactive interpretation.

rules.name: autopoiesis_grounds_value_and_normativity
rules.head: the substrate is a self-producing system
rules.body: inherent norms emerge from need to persist — value isn't added from outside. Weber + Varela. Substrate's drive-as-value.

rules.name: structural_coupling_replaces_representation
rules.head: the substrate maintains persistent coupling with environment
rules.body: no internal model required — coupling itself coordinates behavior. Maturana. Substrate's direct coupling.

rules.name: sense_making_emerges_from_self_maintenance
rules.head: the substrate must maintain its own organization
rules.body: what matters to it (what makes sense) emerges from this. Substrate's drive-grounded meaning.

rules.name: operational_closure_distinguishes_cognitive_systems
rules.head: the substrate has organizational closure
rules.body: it's a candidate cognitive system. Maturana + Varela. Substrate's self-referential closure.
